app-3787fb7725ea465f.upgrade_description:
Upgrade from the public-market v0.22.2 to v0.23.1, adding the Hermes Webapp, configurable subagent delegation, and improvements to conversations, scheduled jobs and plugins.

- Open the Hermes Webapp with its own sign-in. For first-time credentials, run `cat /opt/data/webapp/olares-login.txt` in Hermes CLI. Existing sign-in settings are preserved.
- Use the official `advanced-delegation` plugin to assign subagent tasks to named models or separate profiles. Installing a missing plugin for the first time requires access to GitHub.
- Reset a conversation to the configured default model with `/model reset`, or return to an earlier message and edit or branch the conversation.
- Protect manually curated skills with `hermes curator lock`, cancel running scheduled jobs, and configure how each job handles missed runs.
- Update plugins in bulk or enable optional automatic updates. Fix live plugin-catalog loading above 2 MiB so newly added plugins and current versions can be found.

Compatibility: custom skills using the removed legacy browser tools must use `browser_exec`. MCP clients that launch `hermes mcp serve` must switch to `hermes mcp-serve`.

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/v0.23.0
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/v0.23.1

app-89bcb90267084748.title: [UPDATE][openwebui][1.0.53] Upgrade Open WebUI from 0.13.0 to 0.13.3. Highlights: - Security fixes; upstream strongly recommends updating. - Coding agents such as
app-89bcb90267084748.upgrade_description:
Upgrade Open WebUI from 0.13.0 to 0.13.3. Highlights:
- Security fixes; upstream strongly recommends updating.
- Coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex can appear as models when an Open Terminal offers them, and can run in automations.
- New Auto tool permission mode, where a review model approves safe tool calls.
- Tool chats are much cheaper thanks to prompt caching, and small files are read in full instead of through retrieval.
- Split tab panes, tabs remembered per chat, editable spreadsheets and Markdown, and Git status in the file browser.
- Large chats, channels and the sidebar load faster.
- Fixes for chats, comments and copy buttons when opened over plain HTTP.

Changes to note: this release migrates the database, so back up your data first. Attached files are no longer preloaded into chats by default; models read them with file tools, and models without tool support need Preload files turned on. Retrieval now returns more text by default. Side chats are saved as regular chats.

Release notes: https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/releases/tag/v0.13.3

preview/acestep15v3.head: a2fc82a846bf804f08eed420a795eea92dd201e4
preview/acestep15v3.title: [SUSPEND][acestep15v3][1.1.24] Run the official OpenResty entrance as UID/GID 1000 with writable runtime paths. Switch the reverse-proxy image from Bitnami OpenResty (`beclab/aboveos-bitnami-openresty:1.25.3-2`)
preview/acestep15v3.upgrade_description:
Run the official OpenResty entrance as UID/GID 1000 with writable runtime paths.
Switch the reverse-proxy image from Bitnami OpenResty (`beclab/aboveos-bitnami-openresty:1.25.3-2`) to the official OpenResty image `openresty/openresty:1.29.2.5-bookworm-fat`.

Align nginx config mounts and log paths with the official image layout (`/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`, `/usr/local/openresty/nginx/logs/...`), and drop Bitnami-specific `OPENRESTY_CONF_FILE` wiring.

Bump llm-init image to `beclab/llm-init:v1.3.1`.

Map `HF_TOKEN` / `HF_ENDPOINT` from `OLARES_SYSTEM_HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN` /
`OLARES_SYSTEM_HUGGINGFACE_SERVICE` (system-level), not user-level Hugging Face env.

Move `HF_TOKEN` into a Kubernetes Secret and inject via `secretKeyRef`.

Migrated ACE-Step 1.5 to apiVersion v3 shared app pattern (acestep15v2 → acestep15v3).

**What's Changed**

- **Download architecture**: replaced the bespoke downloader image + Job with
  the shared `llm-init` download-only Deployment (`acestepdownloader`),
  matching speachesv3. Models now land in the shared cross-app HF cache
  (App Common) and the engine gates on the downloader's `/readyz` instead of
  per-repo `.done` sentinels. `/app/checkpoints` is now an ephemeral symlink
  farm over the cached snapshots, so model bytes are de-duplicated and reused
  across apps. Declared `permission.appCommon: true` for the shared HF store.
  Downloader image bumped to `llm-init:v1.3.1` (default LFS; chart no longer
  sets `HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET`).
- **Entrance routing**: rewrote nginx to match speachesv3 — llm-init API paths
  (`/api/progress`, `/healthz`, …) pin to download-svc; `/` gates on model
  download + Gradio readiness and auto-reloads into the app via `/__app_ready`.
- **Resources**: raised nvidia `limitedMemory` to 34Gi so the llm-init downloader
  (4Gi) + engine (29Gi) + entrance (256Mi) limits sum within the envelope.
- **Multi-install**: the acestepweb Deployment now uses {{ .Release.Name }} so allowMultipleInstall installs don't collide on workload names.
- **Accelerator**: declared the GPU requirement via the accelerator modes list (nvidia only; amd64-only app).

- **Architecture**: flattened the acestep15v2/acestep15v2server sub-charts
  into a single chart; renamed the nginx entrance Deployment to `acestep15v3`
  so it matches appid for v3 workload verification. Cross-namespace backend
  references now resolve within the release namespace.
- **Scaling**: `workloadReplicas` declares replica counts for the
  `acestep15v3` entrance and `acestepserver` gradio engine workloads.
  The model-download Job carries no replicas.
- **Runtime**: manual service initialization in Gradio Settings (disabled
  `--service_mode` / `--init_service` auto-load); nvidia `requiredGPUMemory`
  set to 12Gi for acestep-v15-xl-sft + acestep-5Hz-lm-4B.

preview/llamacppqwen3635ba3bggufv3.upgrade_description:
v1.0.26: Store Model Console runtime state in Common. Use existing Common configuration first; otherwise migrate the legacy Cache directory when configuration is available, or initialize new state in Common. Retry shared helper reads during engine startup to tolerate cross-node file updates.

v1.0.24: Model Console (llm-init) updated to v1.7.21.

v1.0.23: Model Console upgrades to llm-init v1.7.19.

v1.0.22: llm-init v1.7.12 — completes the previous fix. A restart now
  prompts the health check to reconsider its schedule immediately, rather
  than waiting out an interval that was already running, which could be
  longer than the whole relaunch. The loading state appears about a second
  after the engine stops rather than seven.
v1.0.21: llm-init v1.7.11 — the engine is checked every second while a
  restart it was asked for is still outstanding. At the steady ten-second
  interval a quick relaunch could take the engine away and give it back
  between two checks, so the phase never moved and a console that had
  just asked for the restart saw nothing at all.
v1.0.20: llm-init v1.7.10 — an engine restart is visible in the model's
  phase while it happens, instead of being hidden by the sixty-second
  grace on a missing engine, and a restart signaled to an engine that
  was already down is confirmed once it comes back rather than reported
  as unverifiable.
v1.0.16: llm-init v1.6.1 — the gate and the capacity reading follow
  ENGINE_ARGS instead of the copy they read at startup. This preset is
  unaffected as shipped, but both directions of an edit now take effect:
  adding -np with -no-kvu gives each slot its own share and the gate
  steps out rather than going on charging two tokenizer hops for a pool
  the engine is already policing, and either way the card reports the
  window and slot count the relaunched engine actually resolved. Before
  this, only restarting the deployment did that.

v1.0.15: llm-init v1.6.0 — this preset names no -np, and llama.cpp's own
  default there is 4 slots sharing one KV pool, not the single slot llm-init
  used to report. So the width Router advertises was wrong, and four slots
  could each claim the whole 131072-token pool. Requests now reserve pool
  room before being forwarded and wait when it is full, answering 503
  kv_budget_exhausted rather than letting the pool run out mid-decode, which
  failed every request generating at that moment. The engine's own /props is
  also read now, so the window and slot count come from what it resolved
  instead of what the flags implied.

preview/vllmgemma412bitawqint4v3.title: [UPDATE][vllmgemma412bitawqint4v3][1.0.25] v1.0.25: Store Model Console runtime state in Common so the console and inference engine can run on different nodes. Use
preview/vllmgemma412bitawqint4v3.upgrade_description:
v1.0.25: Store Model Console runtime state in Common so the console and inference engine can run on different nodes. Use existing Common configuration first; otherwise migrate configuration from the local legacy Cache directory, or initialize new state in Common. Retry shared helper reads during engine startup to tolerate cross-node file updates.

v1.0.24: Model Console (llm-init) updated to v1.7.21.

v1.0.23: Model Console upgrades to llm-init v1.7.19.

v1.0.22: Skip the HuggingFace Hub at startup (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`). Weights are already local when the engine starts, but the read-only cache mount could not hold huggingface_hub's negative cache, so ~90 Hub lookups repeated on every start. Startup 160s → 105s on olarestest01.

v1.0.16: Lower the NVIDIA host-memory reservation so 1.12.6 timeslice nodes can install more easily (engine request 21Gi→6Gi, chart requiredMemory 22Gi→7Gi). GPU quota unchanged.

v1.0.12: ENGINE_ARGS uses the gemma4 tool-call and reasoning parsers.

v1.0.11: bump llm-init to v1.3.5.
v1.0.10: Move `HF_TOKEN` into Kubernetes Secret (`secretKeyRef`); map HF env from `OLARES_SYSTEM_HUGGINGFACE_*`.

v1.0.9: vllm engine add a environment variable HF_HUB_CACHE to point to the shared HF Hub cache.
v1.0.8: VLLM_MEMORY_LIMIT 30Gi; llm-init limit 2Gi; limitedMemory 32Gi (30+2).
v1.0.7: nvidia host memory — requiredMemory 22Gi, VLLM_MEMORY_REQUEST 21Gi, VLLM_MEMORY_LIMIT 26Gi, limitedMemory 30Gi.
v1.0.6: nvidia host memory — requiredMemory 16Gi, VLLM_MEMORY_REQUEST 15Gi, VLLM_MEMORY_LIMIT 19Gi, limitedMemory 26Gi.
v1.0.5: bump llm-init to v1.3.1.
